scope: 17th-century Mediterranean piracy and corsairs; identity, cited claims, contradictions, honest insufficiency
rules: Every expected element below comes from a source that was actually opened while building this set; locators are given per source.
Matchers are accent-, case- and final-sigma-insensitive substring groups: a claim matches when every group has at least one hit.
Only cited claims (research_answer.claims with a source occurrence) count for must_find; uncited prose does not.
Confidence is about the expected answer, not about the historical event: secondary/tertiary sources are marked LOW.
review_status PROPOSED = sourced gold awaiting approval; NEEDS_HISTORIAN = no gold, item is skipped from scoring (scorable=false).

items.query_el: Ποιος ήταν ο Πέτρος Λάντζας (Pedro Lantzas) και σε ποιανού την υπηρεσία βρισκόταν;
items.query_en: Who was Petros Lantzas (Pedro Lantzas) and in whose service was he?

expected_claims.desc: Pedro Lantzas was a Greek agent in Spanish service in the kingdom of Naples (viceroy count of Miranda, 1586-1595); in 1595 he was the channel of secret talks with Piri bey
expected_claims.quote: a través de Pedro Lantzas, agente griego al servicio de los españoles en este reino

expected_claims.desc: Greek scholarship identifies him as the Corfiot Petros Lantzas, governor of Parga (1573) and Spanish agent in Epirus (1596-1608) (titles of Laskaris 1956 and Mertzios 1960 as cited by Floristán n.32)
expected_claims.quote: M. Q. LASKARIS, «Πέτρος Λάντζας, διοικητὴς τῆς Πάργας (1573) καὶ ὄργανον τῶν Ἱσπανῶν ἐν Ἠπείρῳ (1596-1608)» ... K. MERTZIOS, «... ὁ κερκυραῖος Πέτρος Λάντζας»
expected_claims.confidence: MEDIUM (work titles as cited, the Greek studies themselves were not opened)

unresolved_pairs.note: Gürkan 2014 names a 'Pietro Lanza, a skilled corsair in Habsburg employ in 1608'; no opened source states that he is the same man as Pedro Lantzas. Plausible, not established.

forbidden_claims.desc: Placing Lantzas at Milos / in the 1660-1680 Aegean

expected_claims.quote: A similar attempt would be proposed by Pietro Lanza, a skilled corsair in Habsburg employ in 1608
expected_claims.confidence: HIGH (for what the study says; archival original not inspected)

expected_claims.desc: Pedro Lantzas, Greek agent of the Spaniards in Naples, 1595

unresolved_pairs.note: Must be reported as possible, not as established identity.

items.query_el: Ιωάννης Καψής (Jean Capsi, Capsi, Κάψης): ποιος ήταν ο «βασιλιάς της Μήλου»;
items.query_en: Ioannis Kapsis (Jean Capsi, Capsi, Kapsis): who was the 'king of Milos'?

expected_claims.desc: Saulger: Jean Capsi, a Greek of Milo, an experienced seaman, long a pilot on the King's (French) ships, of low birth
expected_claims.quote: Le troisiéme Aventurier fut Jean Capsi; c'étoit un Grec de Milo, qui sçavoit tres bien la mer, & qui avoit été long-tems pilote sur les vaisseaux du Roi (p.319)

expected_claims.desc: He made himself master of the island and the Miliotes accepted him; Tournefort: a Miliote named Capsi set himself up for King of Milo
expected_claims.quote: WE have seen in our days a Miliote, whose Name was Capsi, set himself up for King of Milo (Tournefort p.115)

items.query_el: Hugues Creveliers (Κρεβελιέ, Hugh Cruvelier): ποιος ήταν και πού δρούσε;
items.query_en: Hugues Creveliers (Crevelier, Hugh Cruvelier): who was he and where did he operate?

expected_claims.desc: Saulger: Hugues Creveliers, famous armateur (privateer owner) of La Ciotat in Provence
expected_claims.quote: Le second a été Hugues Creveliers fameux armateur de la Cieutat en Provence (p.305)

expected_claims.desc: Leader of the most important corsair company active in the Aegean in the 1670s
expected_claims.quote: leader of the most important corsair company active in the Aegean sea in the 1670s

expected_claims.desc: Tournefort lists 'Hugh Cruvelier' among the French corsairs (with Temericourt and the Chevalier d'Hocquincourt) whose prizes were brought to Milo

items.query_el: Πώς και πότε τελείωσε η εξουσία του Ιωάννη Καψή στη Μήλο;
items.query_en: How and when did Ioannis Kapsis' rule on Milos end?

expected_claims.desc: The Capitan Pasha sent three galleys on the pretext of collecting the island's annual tribute; Capsi, visiting the commander's galley with only 12 guards, was put in irons
expected_claims.quote: il se contenta d'y envoier trois galéres, sous prétexte de prendre en passant le tribut annuel que paioit l'Isle ... il ne prit avec lui que 12 de ses gardes ... la soldatesque Turque qui avoit le mot, l'entoura de tous côtez, & le mit aux fers (pp.322-323)

expected_claims.desc: Taken to Constantinople and a few days later hanged on a tree before the gate of the Grand Bagne (bagnio), in 1680
expected_claims.quote: mena son prisonnier à Constantinople, où quelques jours aprés il fut pendu à un arbre devant la porte du Grand Bagne l'an 1680 (p.323)

expected_claims.desc: The 'little reign' lasted three years
expected_claims.quote: Ce petit Regne dura trois ans (p.321); after a Reign of three Years (Tournefort p.115)

forbidden_claims.desc: Claiming he was defeated in a sea battle

items.query_el: Ποια επιδρομή του Creveliers στη Λέσβο (Μυτιλήνη) αναφέρεται με ακριβή ημερομηνία;
items.query_en: Which raid by Creveliers on Lesbos (Mytilene) is reported with an exact date?

expected_claims.desc: On 12 March 1676, 800 of his adventurers landed on Metelin in the evening and around midnight scaled the walls of Petra; they left with about 500 captives and rich booty
expected_claims.quote: L'an 1676, le 12 de Mars, 800 de ses Aventuriers débarquez à Mételin sur le soir, traversérent sans bruit trois lieues de païs, & vers le minuit escaladérent le rempart ... ils revinrent avant le jour gagner leurs petits vaisseaux avec 500 esclaves (pp.315-316)

items.query_el: Γιατί φυλακίστηκε ο Πέτρος Λάντζας στη Νάπολη το 1596;
items.query_en: Why was Petros Lantzas imprisoned in Naples in 1596?

expected_claims.desc: After the replacement of viceroy Miranda, Lantzas was imprisoned; letters of the Venetian ambassador in Naples, Gerolamo Ranusio (6 Apr and 27 Aug 1596), blamed him for the resale to the Turks, by the Chimarriotes, of arms the Spanish authorities of Naples had given them for a rising
expected_claims.quote: En Roma le llegó la noticia de la sustitución del virrey Miranda y del encarcelamiento de Lantzas ... se responsabilizó a Lantzas de la reventa que hicieron los chimarrotes a los turcos de las armas (p.196, n.34)
expected_claims.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH (secondary, citing Venetian letters as reported by Laskaris)

items.query_el: Πότε σκοτώθηκε ο Hugues Creveliers στην Αστυπάλαια;
items.query_en: When was Hugues Creveliers killed at Astypalaia?

contradiction.topic: Date of the explosion of Creveliers' ship at Astypalaia (Stampalia)

side_a.quote: Au mois d'Octobre de l'année 1678, il étoit venu mouiller dans le port de Stampalia (pp.316-317)

side_b.quote: Between shortly before midnight of the 24th and early morning of the 25th of September 1679

contradiction.agreed: Both put the explosion of his ship (set off by a member of his crew; Saulger: his valet Adam, a Savoyard) at Astypalaia/Stampalia.

forbidden_claims.desc: Asserting one date as verified without noting the other

items.query_el: Από πού καταγόταν ο Ιωάννης Καψής;
items.query_en: Where did Ioannis Kapsis come from?

side_a.desc: A Greek of Milos / a Miliote (Saulger 1698 p.319; Tournefort 1718 p.115)
side_a.quote: c'étoit un Grec de Milo (Saulger); a Miliote, whose Name was Capsi (Tournefort)

side_b.desc: From Lidoriki in Phocis, with brothers Nikos and 'Kapetan Tromaras' (version attributed to K. Sathas, reported by Stoukas 2018, who also notes the Milos version)
side_b.quote: Η επικρατέστερη εκδοχή όμως, την οποία παρουσιάζει και ο Κ. Σάθας, είναι πως καταγόταν από το Λιδορίκι της Φωκίδας

contradiction.agreed: Both sides agree he became master of Milos and was hanged in Constantinople.

items.query_el: Ποια χρόνια κυβέρνησε τη Μήλο ο Καψής;
items.query_en: In which years did Kapsis rule Milos?

side_a.desc: Hanged in 1680 after a three-year reign (Saulger), i.e. about 1677-1680 (Stoukas 2018: 1677-1680)
side_a.quote: pendu ... l'an 1680; Ce petit Regne dura trois ans

side_b.desc: Arrived 1675, arrested 1678 (Greeka; also calls him George)
side_b.quote: In 1675, a local pirate, George Kapsis, came to Milos ... The Ottomans arrested him in 1678

contradiction.agreed: Both give a short reign of about three years ending in capture and hanging in Constantinople.

pass_criteria.note: A run that reports only the 1680 side with the near-contemporary source and flags uncertainty is acceptable (partial).

items.query_el: Ερεύνησε τη δραστηριότητα πειρατών στη Μήλο μεταξύ 1660 και 1680

expected_claims.desc: Jean Capsi made himself master of Milos and ruled about three years
Capsi was captured by a ruse and hanged in Constantinople in 1680
The Latin bishop Dom Antonio Camillo first recognised him in the Greek cathedral and put a gold chain on his neck
expected_claims.quote: L'Evêque Latin Dom Antonio Camillo fut le premier à le reconnoître dans l'Eglise Cathédrale des Grecs (p.320)

expected_claims.desc: Milos was where French corsairs brought their prizes (the principal fair of the Archipelago); Tournefort names Temericourt, the Chevalier d'Hocquincourt and Hugh Cruvelier
Hugues Creveliers led the most important corsair company in the Aegean in the 1670s (based mainly at Paros per Saulger p.314)

optional_claims.desc: After Capsi's death the Capitan Pasha came with 30 galleys and blew up the Capuchins' hospice on Milos, on the report that it looked like a citadel; Tournefort: their convent was demolished by the Turks on the pretext that they concealed the rovers' plunder. Date after 1680, so out of the 1660-1680 window unless flagged
Neighbouring Argentiere (Kimolos) had been the rendezvous of the French corsairs (Tournefort, Letter IV)

items.query_el: Ερεύνησε τη «βασιλεία» του Ιωάννη Καψή στη Μήλο (1677–1680) με παραπομπές σε πηγές
items.query_en: Research Ioannis Kapsis' 'kingdom' on Milos (1677-1680) with source citations

expected_claims.desc: Greek of Milo, former pilot on the French king's ships (Saulger p.319)
Recognised by the Latin bishop Dom Antonio Camillo, gold chain, people cried 'Vive Capsi' (p.320)
He secured three or four leading islanders not favourable to him, above all one Armeni, the most powerful Greek on Milos (p.320)
Walked among 50 fusiliers; 25-man guard at his door; fixed days to administer justice (pp.320-321)
Captured by a ruse (three galleys, tribute pretext) and hanged in Constantinople before the gate of the Grand Bagne in 1680 (pp.322-323)

expected_claims.quote: the Siphantines, to get rid of 'em at once, gave a Sum of Mony to a Corsair of Provence, who was at Milo, and who cannonaded a second Galliot laden with Jews and Lead-Oar (OCR lines ~14555-14557)
expected_claims.confidence: HIGH for the event as told; the 'About [N] Years ago' date is illegible in OCR

items.query_el: Αποδεικνύεται ότι ο Στάθης Ρωμανός Μανέτας είχε ορμητήριο στους Φούρνους το 1694–1695;
items.query_en: Is it documented that Stathis Romanos Manetas used Phournoi as his base in 1694-1695?
items.premise_status: UNSUPPORTED: Koutsouflakis states no published documentation shows Manetas operating in Phournoi; the Phournoi base is a conjecture based on folk tradition. Right answer: hedge / not documented.
items.gold_quote: No published documentation or official records indicate that Manetas ever conducted operations within the island complex of Phournoi ... whether Stathis Romanos Manetas utilized Phournoi as a base and secure anchorage during his operations in the Chios area in 1694 and 1695 remains a conjecture.

forbidden_claims.desc: Asserting as fact that Manetas used Phournoi as base

items.query_el: Πού παντρεύτηκε και πού σκότωσε τη γυναίκα του ο Μανέτας, κατά την παράδοση; Συμφωνούν οι εκδοχές;
items.query_en: Where, according to tradition, did Manetas marry and kill his wife? Do the versions agree?

contradiction.topic: Place of the Manetas-Marioga episode in folk tradition

side_a.desc: Legend: he married Marioga in Melos and left her in the care of the island's bishop
side_a.quote: Legend has it that he married the beautiful Marioga in Melos, leaving her under the care of the island’s bishop

side_b.desc: Ikarian version: the murder 'in the straits of Samos'; local traditions place it in Ikaria or Phournoi (bays of Pano and Kato Maneta)
side_b.quote: the Ikarian rendition places Manetas’s attempt “in the straits of Samos” ... local traditions suggest that the murder took place either in Ikaria or Phournoi

contradiction.agreed: Folk song (Manetas' rhyme); versions change names and places; none is documentary evidence.

forbidden_claims.desc: Presenting the Marioga story as documented history

items.query_el: Πώς λεγόταν η γυναίκα του Καψή σύμφωνα με τον Saulger;
